pattern.description: A thin rounded strip at the top of the frame grows in width and height (aspect-ratio morph, anchored near the top) into a large empty canvas card; once it settles, the Start node fades in and the cursor glides onto the canvas.
pattern.why_premium: The container itself becomes the transition: the new workspace unfolds from a sliver with a fast-out deceleration (energy peaks on the first frame then decays), so the scene change reads as one continuous object rather than a cut, and content only appears after the frame is stable.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo('.canvas-card', {width: '38%', height: '9%', y: -40}, {width: '80%', height: '67%', y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'expo.out'}).fromTo('.start-node', {autoAlpha: 0}, {autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.2, ease: 'power1.out'}, '-=0.1').to('.cursor', {x: 280, y: -40, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.inOut'}, '<');
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 160, mass: 1}}); width = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [38, 80]) + '%', height = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [9, 67]) + '%'; Start node opacity = interpolate(frame, [10, 16], [0, 1], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); cursor via interpolate with Easing.inOut(Easing.quad).

notes: camera.move is none: the panel changes shape (not a uniform zoom), so this is a container morph, not a camera push. Could alternatively be read as layout_reframe; the earlier shot (e020) shrank the prior window just before this cut.
